chapter: Films, Las Vegas and the union
title: Hazel Scott's pool, a segregated movie theater, and swearing off Las Vegas
summary: He tells of being seated at a bad angle in a theater with Lena Horne, which left him unwilling to return to Las Vegas until 1969.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Wasn't it around that same period that Hazel Scott (I think it was Hazel Scott) decided to take a swim in the pool, and dove into the pool, and they drained the pool?
I heard about that, but I didn't see that.
Well, I just heard about it, too. But that was around that time, wasn't it?

It figures. It had to be around that time. Anyhow, Lena and I one day went downtown to see a show. I think Orson Welles' new picture had just come out, Citizen Kane [sic]. And we went in they show, and they took our money, but when we got in the show they put us way over on the side, so the picture looked like it was coming at you from an angle. So we went back out and got our money back.
And after that engagement I said I'd never go to Las Vegas again, and so I didn't. That was in '47. I didn't go to Las Vegas any more until 1969.
